## Overview

This document pairs each sentinel site with the **Division Provinciale de la
Santé (DPS)** that oversees it, and gives both ends of every pair a
coordinate. It is the input to the question *how accessible is each sentinel
site from its DPS office?*

The work has two point sets and one pairs table:

| Piece | Source | Built by |
|-------|--------|----------|
| Sentinel sites | `../output/drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded_{chain}.csv` | `drc-geocoding-workflow.qmd` |
| DPS seats | `../input/drc_dps.csv` | this document |
| Pairs | `../input/drc_dps_site_pairs.csv` (`network, province, dps, sentinel_site`) | this document |

Sentinel sites are **not** geocoded again here. This document uses the
reviewed output of the sentinel workflow, including its manual overrides.

Like the sentinel sites, every DPS seat is geocoded by every enabled provider,
and two coordinate sets are kept side by side: **`google_first`** and
**`open_first`** (see the sentinel workflow). Each set's DPS seats are paired
with the same set's sentinel sites, so there are two pairs tables.

### Networks

The networks are kept separate, so that accessibility can be compared across
them. Each network holds exactly the pairs its workbook sheet lists:

| Network | Pairs | What it is |
|---------|-------|------------|
| `2003_2005` | 11 | The original sites, named under the 1988–2015 provinces |
| `2014` | 26 | One site per current province |
| `2021_expansion` | 25 | The sites selected in 2021. Kasaï-Central's is still to come |

The 2021 expansion adds to the 2014 network. If you need the full 2021
configuration, combine `2014` and `2021_expansion`.

### How the DPS points are found

Each DPS is geocoded with the same quality gate as the sentinel sites, through
its own query ladder:

1. The office itself: `Division Provinciale de la Sante <province>`, pinned to the province
2. The chef-lieu town, pinned to the province
3. The chef-lieu, province and country as free text
4. The chef-lieu alone, restricted to the country

Every rung's result is matched against the **chef-lieu name**. So an office
result in the wrong town is refused by the gate. What the gate cannot do with
Google is tell the DPS office from another building in the right town, because
Google returns no establishment name. **Every unnamed building therefore goes
to review**, however high its confidence. To confirm one, pin it in
`../input/dps_manual_overrides.csv`.

OpenStreetMap names its buildings, so an open provider's answer to the office
query must also be **named like the office**. Photon's answer for DPS
Haut-Katanga, a church in Lubumbashi, is refused for that reason. A building
that passes is labelled `office` and, unlike an unnamed building, needs no
review on that account.

GRID3 lists no DPS offices, so it answers only the chef-lieu rung, and only
where the chef-lieu is also a settlement in the health zone of the same name.

## Setup

```{r}
#| label: load-libraries
#| eval: true

library(tidyverse)
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
library(leaflet)
library(htmlwidgets)
library(knitr)

knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = knitr::is_html_output())

source("config.R")
source("geocode-functions.R")
source("providers.R")
source("pairs-functions.R")

dir.create(paths$output, showWarnings = FALSE, recursive = TRUE)
```

Credentials are read from the environment and are never printed or written.
They are needed only for requests that are not already cached.

```{r}
#| label: api-key-check
#| eval: true

credential_status() |>
  kable(caption = "Credentials for the enabled providers")
```

## Inputs

### DPS seats

The registry holds DPS seats. `province` is the current province the seat lies
in, which the gate checks. `chef_lieu` is the town the office is in, and it is
the name every candidate is matched against.

It lists the 26 current DPS and 5 pre-2015 DPS whose provinces no longer exist
(Bandundu, Bas-Congo, Kasaï Occidental, Katanga and Province Orientale). Every
pre-2015 seat is also a current chef-lieu. The other six pre-2015 DPS
(Équateur, Kasaï Oriental, Kinshasa, Maniema, Nord-Kivu and Sud-Kivu) have the
same name and seat as a current DPS, so their pairs use that DPS's row.

```{r}
#| label: dps-input
#| eval: true

dps <- read.csv(paths$dps_input, stringsAsFactors = FALSE) |>
  ensure_site_id(dps_profile) |>
  distinct(dps_id, .keep_all = TRUE)

validate_provinces(dps)
cat("DPS headquarters:", nrow(dps), "| provinces:", length(unique(dps$province)), "\n")

dps |>
  select(dps_id, dps, province, chef_lieu) |>
  kable(caption = "DPS seats to geocode")
```

### Pairs and sentinel sites

Each pair records its `province` as the network named it. The 2003–2005
pairs therefore use the 1988–2015 provinces. When the pairs are built, both
ends of a pair must lie in what its province became in the July 2015 split
(`provinces_pre2015` in `config.R`). If either end does not, the build stops.

```{r}
#| label: pairs-input
#| eval: true

pairs_in <- read.csv(paths$pairs, stringsAsFactors = FALSE,
                     colClasses = c(network = "character"))

sites <- map(names(chains) |> set_names(), function(ch) {
  path <- file.path(paths$output, sprintf("drc_sentinel_sites_geocoded_%s.csv", ch))
  if (!file.exists(path)) {
    stop("Sentinel site coordinates not found at ", path,
         ". Render drc-geocoding-workflow.qmd first.")
  }
  read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
})

pairs_in |>
  count(network, name = "pairs") |>
  kable(caption = "Pairs by network")

imap(sites, \(s, ch) count(s, confidence) |> mutate(chain = ch)) |>
  list_rbind() |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = chain, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  kable(caption = "Sentinel site coordinates by confidence, per set")
```

## Geocoding the DPS Headquarters

### Query ladder

```{r}
#| label: dps-ladder-example
#| eval: true

build_query_variants("Kananga", "Kasaï-Central", ladder = ladders$dps) |>
  select(rung, rung_label, address, components, target) |>
  kable(caption = "DPS query ladder, for DPS Kasaï-Central")
```

### Processing loop

```{r}
#| label: dps-processing-loop
#| eval: true

n_cached <- cache_load()
cat("Cached responses available:",
    paste0(names(n_cached), " ", n_cached, collapse = ", "), "\n\n")

answers <- list()
audits  <- list()

for (i in seq_len(nrow(dps))) {
  row <- dps[i, ]
  out <- geocode_point_all(
    site_id   = row$dps_id,
    site      = row$chef_lieu,
    province  = row$province,
    point_set = "dps"
  )
  answers[[i]] <- out$by_provider
  audits[[i]]  <- out$audit
  cache_save()   # an interrupted run keeps what it has fetched

  cat(sprintf("[%2d/%2d] %-20s %-12s %s\n", i, nrow(dps), row$dps, row$chef_lieu,
              paste0(out$by_provider$provider, ":", out$by_provider$confidence,
                     collapse = " ")))
}

dps_by_provider <- bind_rows(answers) |> rename(dps_id = site_id)
dps_candidates  <- bind_rows(audits)  |> rename(dps_id = site_id)

cache_save()
dps_stats <- cache_stats() |> filter(provider %in% enabled_providers())
cat("\nRequests per provider:",
    paste0(dps_stats$provider, " ", dps_stats$requests, collapse = ", "),
    "| served from cache:", sum(dps_stats$cache_hits), "\n")
```

### Coordinate sets, manual overrides and review

A row goes to review if any of these is true:

- It was not resolved at high confidence.
- It resolved to anything other than a town or neighbourhood centroid, unless it
  was pinned by hand or is a building named as the office. For example, an
  unnamed building that may or may not be the DPS office.
- The other providers do not confirm it: one of them put the seat more than
  `r crosscheck$agree_km` km away, or none found it.

```{r}
#| label: dps-overrides-review
#| eval: true

review_reason <- function(d) {
  d |> mutate(review_reason = case_when(
    confidence == "failed"          ~ "no acceptable candidate",
    confidence == "manual" & crosscheck == "disagree" ~
      sprintf("pinned, but a provider puts it %.0f km away", max_disagreement_km),
    confidence == "manual"          ~ NA_character_,
    point_basis == "establishment"  ~ "building in the right town: confirm it is the DPS office",
    point_basis == "other"          ~ "resolved to a street or other non-settlement",
    confidence != "high"            ~ paste0(
      confidence, " confidence, rung ", resolved_at_rung,
      if_else(coalesce(quality_flags, "") != "", paste0(": ", quality_flags), "")
    ),
    crosscheck == "disagree"        ~ sprintf("providers disagree by up to %.0f km",
                                              max_disagreement_km),
    crosscheck == "single-source"   ~ "no other source confirms it",
    TRUE                            ~ NA_character_
  ))
}

dps_finals <- map(chains, function(ch) {
  chosen <- dps_by_provider |>
    select_chain(ch, id_col = "dps_id") |>
    apply_manual_overrides(paths$dps_overrides, id_col = "dps_id") |>
    crosscheck_points(dps_by_provider, id_col = "dps_id") |>
    mutate(point_basis = case_when(
      geocode_status == "manual" ~ "manual",
      # The gate held a named building from the office rung to the office name
      matched_kind == "establishment" & geocode_status != "google" &
        ladders$dps$target[resolved_at_rung] == "office" ~ "office",
      TRUE ~ matched_kind
    ))
  dps |> left_join(chosen, by = "dps_id") |> review_reason()
})

for (ch in names(dps_finals)) {
  write.csv(dps_finals[[ch]], file.path(paths$output, sprintf("drc_dps_geocoded_%s.csv", ch)),
            row.names = FALSE)
  write.csv(dps_finals[[ch]] |> filter(!is.na(review_reason)),
            file.path(paths$output, sprintf("drc_dps_review_%s.csv", ch)), row.names = FALSE)
}
write.csv(dps |> select(dps_id, dps, province, chef_lieu) |>
            right_join(dps_by_provider, by = "dps_id"),
          file.path(paths$output, "drc_dps_by_provider.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(dps_candidates, file.path(paths$output, "drc_dps_candidates.csv"), row.names = FALSE)
write.csv(dps_stats |> mutate(point_set = "dps", .before = 1),
          file.path(paths$output, "drc_dps_provider_stats.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

dps_all <- imap(dps_finals, \(d, ch) mutate(d, chain = ch, .before = 1)) |> list_rbind()

cat("Manual overrides applied:", sum(dps_finals[[1]]$confidence == "manual"), "\n")
dps_all |>
  group_by(chain) |>
  summarise(review = sum(!is.na(review_reason)), of = n(),
            from_google = sum(geocode_status == "google", na.rm = TRUE)) |>
  kable(caption = "Review queue and Google-sourced seats per set")

dps_all |>
  count(chain, point_basis, confidence) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = chain, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  kable(caption = "DPS coordinates by basis and confidence")

dps_by_provider |>
  count(provider, confidence) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = confidence, values_from = n, values_fill = 0) |>
  arrange(match(provider, names(providers))) |>
  kable(caption = "What each provider found on its own")

dps_all |>
  mutate(answer = if_else(is.na(latitude), "failed",
                          sprintf("%s r%s %s (%s)", geocode_status,
                                  coalesce(as.character(resolved_at_rung), "-"),
                                  confidence, crosscheck))) |>
  select(chain, dps, chef_lieu, answer) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = chain, values_from = answer) |>
  kable(caption = "DPS geocoding results: source, rung, tier and cross-check per set")
```

```{r}
#| label: dps-review-table
#| eval: true

dps_review <- dps_all |> filter(!is.na(review_reason))
if (nrow(dps_review) > 0) {
  dps_review |>
    select(chain, dps, chef_lieu, geocode_status, point_basis, confidence,
           matched_address, review_reason) |>
    kable(caption = "DPS review queue")
} else {
  cat("Nothing to review.\n")
}
```

## Pairs

`straight_line_km` is a great-circle distance, not a travel distance. It is here
to catch blunders and to show which pairs are **co-located**, meaning under
1 km apart. That usually means the sentinel site is in the DPS town itself, and
both ends were resolved to the same town centroid. A pair whose ends come from
different providers is rarely under 1 km even when the site is in the DPS town,
because providers put a town's point in different places.

```{r}
#| label: build-pairs
#| eval: true

ods <- map(names(chains) |> set_names(),
           \(ch) build_pairs(pairs_in, dps_finals[[ch]], sites[[ch]]))

for (ch in names(ods)) {
  write.csv(ods[[ch]], file.path(paths$output, sprintf("drc_dps_site_pairs_%s.csv", ch)),
            row.names = FALSE)
  cat(sprintf("Pairs saved to: output/drc_dps_site_pairs_%s.csv\n", ch))
}

od_all <- imap(ods, \(o, ch) mutate(o, chain = ch, .before = 1)) |> list_rbind()

od_all |>
  group_by(chain, network) |>
  summarise(
    pairs              = n(),
    complete           = sum(complete),
    co_located         = sum(co_located),
    dps_office         = sum(dps_basis == "office", na.rm = TRUE),
    dps_establishment  = sum(dps_basis == "establishment", na.rm = TRUE),
    dps_settlement     = sum(dps_basis == "settlement", na.rm = TRUE),
    dps_manual         = sum(dps_basis == "manual", na.rm = TRUE),
    open_both_ends     = sum(complete & dps_source != "google" & site_source != "google"),
    province_mismatch  = sum(province_mismatch),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  kable(caption = "Pairs by set and network")
```

### Province changes

This section covers networks named under the 1988–2015 provinces. It shows how
each pair's province maps onto today's provinces. When a province was split in
2015, the site and its former DPS seat usually stayed in the same new province.
Where they did not, the pair is flagged `province_mismatch`. The site now
belongs to a different DPS, which a later network pairs it with. None of this
depends on the coordinate set.

```{r}
#| label: province-changes
#| eval: true

old_networks <- ods[[1]] |>
  group_by(network) |>
  filter(any(!normalise_name(network_province) %in% normalise_name(drc_provinces))) |>
  ungroup()

if (nrow(old_networks) > 0) {
  old_networks |>
    mutate(
      n_successors = map_int(network_province, \(p) length(successor_provinces(p))),
      change = case_when(
        n_successors == 1 &
          normalise_name(network_province) == normalise_name(site_province) ~ "unchanged",
        n_successors == 1                                                   ~ "renamed",
        !province_mismatch ~ "split; seat and site in the same new province",
        TRUE               ~ "split; seat and site now in different provinces"
      )
    ) |>
    transmute(network, then = network_province, dps, seat = chef_lieu,
              seat_now = dps_province, sentinel_site, site_now = site_province,
              change) |>
    kable(caption = "Pre-2015 pairs on today's provinces")
} else {
  cat("No network uses pre-2015 province names.\n")
}
```

### Network comparison

The table below shows sites paired in more than one network, with each
network's DPS seat and the straight-line distance between them, in each set.

```{r}
#| label: network-comparison
#| eval: true

shared <- od_all |>
  group_by(chain, site_id) |>
  filter(n_distinct(network) > 1) |>
  ungroup()

if (nrow(shared) > 0) {
  shared |>
    transmute(chain, sentinel_site, network, seat = chef_lieu,
              km = round(straight_line_km, 1)) |>
    pivot_wider(names_from = network, values_from = c(seat, km),
                names_glue = "{.value}_{network}", names_sort = TRUE) |>
    arrange(sentinel_site, chain) |>
    kable(caption = "Sites paired in more than one network")
} else {
  cat("No site is paired in more than one network.\n")
}
```

### Incomplete pairs

Both sets hold every provider, so they lack coordinates for the same points.

```{r}
#| label: incomplete-pairs
#| eval: true

incomplete <- ods[[1]] |> filter(!complete)
if (nrow(incomplete) > 0) {
  incomplete |>
    select(network, dps, sentinel_site, dps_confidence, site_confidence) |>
    kable(caption = "Pairs missing a coordinate at one end")
} else {
  cat("Every pair has coordinates at both ends.\n")
}
```

### Co-located pairs

```{r}
#| label: co-located-pairs
#| eval: true

co_loc <- od_all |> filter(co_located)
if (nrow(co_loc) > 0) {
  co_loc |>
    select(chain, network, dps, chef_lieu, sentinel_site, dps_basis, straight_line_km) |>
    mutate(straight_line_km = round(straight_line_km, 2)) |>
    kable(caption = "Pairs under 1 km apart")
} else {
  cat("No co-located pairs.\n")
}
```

### All pairs

One row per pair, with its distance and its ends' sources in each set. The
coordinates are in the pairs files.

```{r}
#| label: all-pairs
#| eval: true

od_all |>
  transmute(
    chain, network, province = network_province, dps, sentinel_site,
    km = round(straight_line_km, 1),
    sources = if_else(complete, paste(dps_source, site_source, sep = " / "), "incomplete")
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(names_from = chain, values_from = c(km, sources),
              names_glue = "{.value}_{chain}") |>
  kable(caption = "DPS–site pairs (sources: DPS end / site end)")
```

## Map

Each set is a group of layers; `open_first` is shown, and `google_first` can be
switched on.

```{r}
#| label: pairs-map
#| eval: true
#| fig-cap: "DPS headquarters and sentinel sites, joined by pair."

networks <- sort(unique(od_all$network))   # chronological: names start with a year
net_cols <- setNames(rep_len(c("#4d4d4d", "#e08214", "#542788"), length(networks)),
                     networks)

map <- leaflet() |> addTiles()
groups <- character(0)

for (ch in names(chains)) {
  lines <- ods[[ch]] |> filter(complete)

  # Several DPS can share a seat (DPS Kwilu and the pre-2015 DPS Bandundu are
  # both in Bandundu), so draw one marker per seat with every DPS in its label.
  seats <- dps_finals[[ch]] |>
    filter(!is.na(latitude)) |>
    group_by(latitude, longitude, chef_lieu) |>
    summarise(dps = paste(dps, collapse = " / "),
              point_basis = first(point_basis), confidence = first(confidence),
              source = first(geocode_status), crosscheck = first(crosscheck),
              matched_address = first(matched_address), .groups = "drop")

  g_dps   <- paste0("DPS (", ch, ")")
  g_sites <- paste0("Sentinel sites (", ch, ")")
  g_pairs <- paste0("Pairs ", networks, " (", ch, ")")
  groups  <- c(groups, g_dps, g_sites, g_pairs)

  map <- map |>
    addCircleMarkers(
      data = seats,
      lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude, group = g_dps,
      color = "#b2182b", radius = 7, fillOpacity = 0.8,
      label = ~dps,
      popup = ~paste0("<b>", dps, "</b> (", ch, ")<br>",
                      "<b>Chef-lieu:</b> ", chef_lieu, "<br>",
                      "<b>Source:</b> ", source, "<br>",
                      "<b>Basis:</b> ", point_basis, "<br>",
                      "<b>Confidence:</b> ", confidence, "<br>",
                      "<b>Cross-check:</b> ", crosscheck, "<br>",
                      "<b>Matched address:</b> ", matched_address)
    ) |>
    addCircleMarkers(
      data = sites[[ch]] |> filter(!is.na(latitude)),
      lng = ~longitude, lat = ~latitude, group = g_sites,
      color = "#2166ac", radius = 5, fillOpacity = 0.8,
      label = ~sentinel_site,
      popup = ~paste0("<b>", sentinel_site, "</b> (", ch, ")<br>",
                      "<b>Province:</b> ", province, "<br>",
                      "<b>Source:</b> ", geocode_status, "<br>",
                      "<b>Confidence:</b> ", confidence)
    )

  for (i in seq_len(nrow(lines))) {
    map <- map |>
      addPolylines(lng = c(lines$dps_lon[i], lines$site_lon[i]),
                   lat = c(lines$dps_lat[i], lines$site_lat[i]),
                   color = net_cols[[lines$network[i]]], weight = 2, opacity = 0.7,
                   group = paste0("Pairs ", lines$network[i], " (", ch, ")"),
                   label = paste0(lines$network[i], ": ", lines$dps[i], " → ",
                                  lines$sentinel_site[i], ", ",
                                  round(lines$straight_line_km[i], 1), " km"))
  }
}

map <- map |>
  addLayersControl(overlayGroups = groups,
                   options = layersControlOptions(collapsed = FALSE)) |>
  hideGroup(groups[grepl("google_first", groups)])

# Build in a temp directory: saveWidget() leaves a scratch "*_files" folder
# beside its target even when the result is fully self-contained.
staged <- file.path(tempdir(), "drc_dps_site_pairs_map.html")
saveWidget(map, staged, selfcontained = TRUE)
file.copy(staged, file.path(paths$output, "drc_dps_site_pairs_map.html"), overwrite = TRUE)

map
```

## Extending to Other Networks

A network is a set of rows in `../input/drc_dps_site_pairs.csv`, tagged with
its `network`. Both of its points must be in a registry first.

All three networks are paired:

- **2003–2005 and 2014.** All 11 original sites are among the 26. The 2003–2005
  pairs name the 1988–2015 provinces, and `provinces_pre2015` maps those onto
  today's provinces.
- **2021_expansion.** Its 25 sites are in their own input,
  `../input/drc_sentinel_sites_2021_expansion.csv`, which the sentinel workflow
  geocodes along with the 26.

When Kasaï-Central's 2021 site is chosen:

1. Add a row to `drc_sentinel_sites_2021_expansion.csv`.
2. Re-render `drc-geocoding-workflow.qmd`.
3. Add the pair row: `2021_expansion, Kasaï-Central, DPS Kasaï-Central, <site>`.

A later network works the same way:

1. Put its new sites in a new input file and add that file to `paths$input` in
   `config.R`.
2. Add its pair rows under a name that starts with its year.

If a pair names a site that has not been geocoded, the build stops and lists it.

## Output Files

| File | Description |
|:-------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| `drc_dps_site_pairs_{chain}.csv` | One row per pair: both coordinates, their sources, provenance, straight-line km and flags |
| `drc_dps_geocoded_{chain}.csv` | DPS input columns plus coordinates, basis (office/establishment/settlement/manual), cross-check and review reason |
| `drc_dps_review_{chain}.csv` | DPS to check by hand |
| `drc_dps_by_provider.csv` | Every provider's own answer for every DPS seat |
| `drc_dps_candidates.csv` | Every DPS candidate at every rung, from every provider, accepted or rejected |
| `drc_dps_provider_stats.csv` | Requests and cache hits per provider for this run |
| `drc_dps_site_pairs_map.html` | Interactive map of the pairs in both sets |

`{chain}` is `google_first` or `open_first`. Outputs are git-ignored. Commit a
deliverable deliberately, with `git add -f`. Google's terms allow its
coordinates to be cached for 30 days and not published, so only pairs whose
ends both come from open sources (`dps_source` and `site_source` other than
`google`) can be shared.
